_comment: Stowage tiers — see docs/minigame-stowage.md §4. 'dunnage' is the real difficulty dial: an empty rectangle is the friendliest packing problem there is, because its borders and corners are perfect anchors, and wedging timber into the middle turns every one of those anchors into a question. 'goods' and the grid are volume knobs — they make a crate longer, not harder — so they climb far more gently. Free slots must divide into 'goods' parts that all land inside [minSlots, maxSlots]: w*h - dunnage over goods is 5.0 / 4.25 / 4.1 here, which keeps every part in range with room either side. 6x7 is the ceiling at which a slot stays a comfortable tap target in portrait.
